answer: Each agent can open only one escrow-backed account per independently verified device credential. Before trading, it locks a bond that is forfeited if the account is caught coordinating fraudulent claims; honest users recover it after a dispute window. A fraudster cannot multiply voting or credit by minting accounts, because duplicate credentials map to one account, while obtaining distinct devices and bonds raises the attack cost. A ridge of independent reviewers can flag linked behavior, but the bond, not a name like opal or lotus, makes repeated identities expensive.
